The problem with this is that you would be the only VPN user on your VPS. While this does mitigate the threat of the VPN service logging your traffic, it opens you up to a new threat model wherein your traffic is easier to distinguish than a random VPN user on a multi-user service.

Using a VPN service will make it harder for external adversaries to slurp your data over the wire, but you are at the mercy of the service provider. Also, adversarial groups looking to harvest massive amounts of data will find it more attractive to infiltrate the network of a service provider, rather than your personal VPS.

However, if you're just trying to get around a national firewall, then rolling your own VPN is probably the better option, unless you're a high-profile individual.
